Cumulative, beginner-facing, grouped by the week each term is covered (not A–Z). `/course-notes add` appends a `## Week N` section. Never delete an existing entry; a later week may add a stricter-sense note, but the original beginner anchor stays. One sentence plus a cross-reference to the week section that introduces the term.

## Week 1

- **High energy physics.** The discovery and measurement of the fundamental constituents of matter and their basic interactions. See [What high energy physics is](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-hep).
- **Beam and target.** The particles aimed at something, and the thing they hit; in a collider the target is the other beam. See [Anatomy of an experiment](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-anatomy).
- **Detector.** The part of an experiment that records what comes out of a collision. See [Anatomy of an experiment](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-anatomy).
- **Data acquisition (DAQ).** The electronics and computing that read the detector out and store the data. See [Anatomy of an experiment](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-anatomy).
- **Hermetic detector.** A detector that surrounds the collision point as completely as possible. See [One structure at two scales](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-rutherford).
- **Luminosity ($\mathcal{L}$).** The factor that turns a cross section into an interaction rate; developed in Week 2. See [Accelerators, detectors and analysis](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-three).
- **Cross section ($\sigma$).** An effective area for a process. See [Accelerators, detectors and analysis](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-three).
- **Resolution.** How finely a detector measures a quantity; for momentum, $\sigma/p$. See [Accelerators, detectors and analysis](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-three).
- **Signal and background.** The kind of event we look for, and the events that look similar enough to be mistaken for it. See [Accelerators, detectors and analysis](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-three).
- **Pseudorapidity ($\eta$).** A label for the angle from the beam axis, $\eta=-\ln\tan(\theta/2)$. See [CDF at the Tevatron](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-cdf).
- **Dark matter direct detection.** Searching for a dark matter particle scattering in a detector. See [An energy ladder](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-ladder).
- **WIMP.** A weakly interacting massive particle, the candidate in such searches. See [An energy ladder](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-ladder).
- **Neutrinoless double beta decay.** A hypothetical decay searched for as a sharp line at the end of the double beta decay spectrum. See [An energy ladder](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-ladder).
- **CEvNS.** Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, in which a neutrino scatters from a nucleus as a whole. See [An energy ladder](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-ladder).
- **Phonon.** A quantum of vibration in a crystal, read out by some low-energy detectors. See [An energy ladder](lectures/week01.qmd#sec-ladder).

## Week 2

- **Dipole.** A magnet with a uniform field that bends the beam onto a circular arc. See [Bending with a dipole](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-dipole).
- **Bending radius ($\rho$).** The radius of the arc a beam of momentum $p$ follows in a field $B$, $\rho = p/0.3B$ in GeV/$c$, tesla and metres. See [Bending with a dipole](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-dipole).
- **Magnetic rigidity ($B\rho$).** The beam's momentum expressed as a magnetic quantity. See [Bending with a dipole](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-dipole).
- **Quadrupole.** A four-pole magnet whose field grows linearly with distance from the axis, focusing in one plane and defocusing in the other. See [Focusing with a quadrupole](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-quad).
- **Field gradient ($g$).** The rate $\partial B_y/\partial x$ at which a quadrupole's field grows with distance from the axis. See [Focusing with a quadrupole](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-quad).
- **Weak and strong focusing.** Weak focusing uses one magnet to bend and focus; strong focusing alternates focusing and defocusing quadrupoles. See [Weak and strong focusing](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-strong).
- **FODO lattice.** A repeating sequence of focusing (F), drift (O) and defocusing (D) elements that gives net focusing. See [Weak and strong focusing](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-strong).
- **Focal length ($F$).** The distance at which a thin lens brings a parallel ray to the axis. See [The quadrupole as a thin lens](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-thinlens).
- **Reference orbit.** The ideal closed path of a particle of the design momentum. See [Describing motion about the reference orbit](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-coords).
- **Focusing strength ($K$).** The field gradient divided by the momentum, $K=(e/p)\,\partial B_y/\partial x$. See [The equations of motion](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-eom).
- **Transfer matrix.** A matrix that maps a particle's $(x, x')$ at one position to its value further downstream. See [Transfer matrices](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-matrices).
- **Hill's equation.** $u''+K(s)u=0$ with $K$ periodic around the ring. See [Beam envelope and emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-envelope).
- **Betatron oscillation.** The transverse oscillation of a particle about the reference orbit. See [Beam envelope and emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-envelope).
- **Betatron function ($\beta(s)$).** The machine function that sets the beam envelope, $\sigma=\sqrt{\epsilon\beta}$. See [Beam envelope and emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-envelope).
- **Courant-Snyder parameters ($\alpha,\beta,\gamma$).** The three functions of $s$ that describe the shape and orientation of the phase-space ellipse. See [Beam envelope and emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-envelope).
- **Emittance ($\epsilon$).** The size of a beam in transverse phase space, the value of the Courant-Snyder invariant. See [Beam envelope and emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-envelope).
- **Tune ($\nu$).** The number of betatron oscillations per revolution. See [Tune and resonances](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-tune).
- **Resonance.** A tune condition $p\nu_x+q\nu_y=$ integer at which small errors add up turn after turn. See [Tune and resonances](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-tune).
- **Luminosity ($\mathcal{L}$).** The factor that converts a cross section into an interaction rate. See [Luminosity](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-lumi).
- **$\beta^*$.** The value of the betatron function at the collision point. See [Luminosity in terms of emittance](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-lumi-eps).
- **Tune shift ($\Delta\nu$).** The change in tune caused by extra focusing, in colliders mainly from the other beam. See [The beam-beam force and the tune shift](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-beambeam).
- **Centre-of-mass energy ($\sqrt{s}$).** The energy available for making new particles. See [Why colliders?](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-why).
- **RF (radio-frequency) cavity.** A resonant cavity whose alternating longitudinal field accelerates the beam. See [The basics of acceleration](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-accel).
- **Harmonic number ($h$).** The number of places around the ring where a particle can arrive in time with the RF field. See [Orbit length and RF frequency](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-rf).
- **Synchronous phase ($\phi_s$).** The RF phase at which the reference particle arrives. See [Phase stability and transition](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-transition).
- **Transition energy ($\gamma_T$).** The energy at which the sign of the arrival-time change with momentum flips. See [Phase stability and transition](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-transition).
- **RF bucket and separatrix.** The region of stable longitudinal motion and the curve that bounds it. See [Phase space of stable oscillations](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-bucket).
- **Synchrotron oscillation.** The oscillation of a particle in energy and phase about the reference particle. See [Synchrotron oscillations](lectures/week02.qmd#sec-synchro).

## Week 3

- **Synchrotron radiation.** The radiation a relativistic charged particle emits when its path is bent, as in a dipole. See [Synchrotron radiation](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-sr).
- **Larmor formula.** The radiated power of an accelerated charge; for a bent relativistic particle $P_\gamma \propto \beta^4\gamma^4/\rho^2$. See [Synchrotron radiation](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-sr).
- **Lorentz factor ($\gamma$).** The ratio $E/mc^2$ of a particle's energy to its rest energy. See [Synchrotron radiation](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-sr).
- **Energy loss per turn ($U_0$).** The energy a particle radiates on one trip around a ring, which the RF must restore, $U_0 \propto \gamma^4/\rho$. See [Energy lost per turn](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-sr-turn).
- **Parton.** A quark or gluon inside a proton; a proton collision is really a collision of one parton from each proton. See [Electrons, protons and muons](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-species).
- **Linear collider.** A collider that accelerates two beams in straight linacs and collides each bunch once. See [Linear colliders](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-linear).
- **Accelerating gradient.** The energy a particle gains per metre of accelerating structure, in MV/m. See [Linear colliders](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-linear).
- **Beamstrahlung.** Radiation a particle emits in the field of the oncoming bunch, which spreads the collision energies below the nominal value. See [The energy spread of the collisions](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-spread).
- **Muon collider.** A collider of muons, point-like like electrons but radiating about $10^9$ times less; its muons decay with a rest lifetime of about 2.2 $\mu$s. See [Muon colliders](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-muon).
- **Time dilation.** The lengthening of a moving particle's lifetime in the laboratory to $\gamma\tau$. See [Muon colliders](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-muon).
- **Muon beam halo.** Background in a muon collider detector from the products of muons decaying near the interaction region. See [Muon colliders](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-muon).
- **Beam screen.** A liner inside the beam pipe of a superconducting ring that intercepts synchrotron radiation at a temperature where cooling is cheaper. See [Synchrotron radiation in a hadron ring](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-screens).
- **Critical photon energy.** A characteristic energy of the synchrotron photons a beam emits. See [Synchrotron radiation in a hadron ring](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-screens).
- **Pileup ($\mu$).** The extra collisions in the same bunch crossing as the one of interest, with mean $\mu = \mathcal{L}\sigma_{\text{inel}}/f_{\text{BC}}$. See [Pileup](lectures/week03.qmd#sec-pileup).

## Week 4

- **Rare event search.** An experiment looking for a process expected only a few times per year in tens or hundreds of kilograms of detector, such as WIMP scattering, neutrinoless double beta decay or CEvNS. See [Rare event searches](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-rare).
- **Exposure.** Detector mass times live time, for example in kg·day; the number of events of a rare process grows in proportion to it. See [Background and the DRU](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-dru).
- **Region of interest (ROI).** The window of deposited energy in which the signal is expected. See [Background and the DRU](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-dru).
- **DRU.** The differential rate unit, one event per keV per kg per day, used to compare background levels between experiments. See [Background and the DRU](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-dru).
- **Noise (versus background).** Continuous fluctuations, usually not from particle interactions; background, by contrast, gives pulses from particle interactions. See [Noise and background](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-noise-bg).
- **Reduced mass ($m_r$).** $m_\chi m_N/(m_\chi + m_N)$, the mass that sets the kinematics of a WIMP-nucleus collision. See [The signal rate](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-rate).
- **Form factor ($F$).** The factor by which scattering from a nucleus falls below coherent scattering once the momentum transfer resolves the nucleus's size. See [The nuclear structure factor](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-rate-nuclear).
- **Spin-independent scattering.** WIMP-nucleus scattering in which the amplitudes from all nucleons add coherently, so the cross section grows as $A^2$. See [The particle physics factor](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-rate-particle).
- **Energy threshold.** The smallest deposited energy a detector can reliably record. See [Exposure and threshold](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-exposure-threshold).
- **Electron recoil (ER) and nuclear recoil (NR).** A scatter from an atomic electron (gammas, betas) or from a nucleus (WIMPs, neutrons, CEvNS). See [Signal against background](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-er-nr).
- **Cosmogenic background.** Background induced by cosmic rays, such as fast neutrons from muon spallation. See [Signal against background](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-er-nr).
- **Material assay.** Measuring the radioactive contamination of a material, often at parts per billion, before it is used in a detector. See [Step 1: radiopure materials](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-radiopure).
- **Metres water equivalent (m.w.e.).** Depth underground expressed as the depth of water that would stop muons equally well. See [Step 2: going underground](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-underground).
- **Passive and active shielding.** Material that absorbs radiation (lead, polyethylene, water), and detectors that tag it so events can be vetoed (muon and neutron vetoes). See [Step 3: shielding](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-shielding).
- **Ionization yield ($Y$).** The ionization energy of an event divided by its phonon energy, near 1 for electron recoils and lower for nuclear recoils. See [Particle identification from the detector response](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-response).
- **Surface events and fiducialization.** Events near a detector surface with incomplete charge collection, removed by keeping only an inner (fiducial) volume. See [Particle identification from the detector response](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-response).
- **Annual modulation.** The yearly variation in a WIMP signal caused by the Earth's orbit through the dark matter halo. See [Astrophysical modulation](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-modulation).
- **Noise spectral density.** Noise per $\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ of bandwidth, in V/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ or A/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$. See [Reading a noise spectrum](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-psd).
- **Johnson–Nyquist noise.** Thermal noise in a resistor, $v_n = \sqrt{4k_BTR\Delta f}$, reduced by cooling. See [Types of noise](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-noise-types).
- **Shot noise.** Noise from the discreteness of the charges in a current, $i_n = \sqrt{2Iq\Delta f}$. See [Types of noise](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-noise-types).
- **Heat capacity ($C$).** The energy needed to raise an object's temperature by one kelvin; at low temperature $\propto T$ for electrons and $\propto T^3$ for phonons. See [Specific heat](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-heatcap).
- **Thermal conductivity ($\kappa$).** The constant in Fourier's law $\dot q = -\kappa\nabla T$; the heat flow along a rod is $(A/L)\int\kappa\,dT$. See [Thermal conductivity](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-conduct).
- **Kapitza resistance.** The thermal resistance of a boundary between two materials, from an acoustic mismatch for phonons. See [Thermal conductivity](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-conduct).
- **Wiedemann–Franz law.** For a metal, $\kappa/\sigma = L_0T$, linking thermal and electrical conductivity. See [The Wiedemann–Franz law](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-wf).
- **Residual-resistance ratio (RRR).** $R_{300\,\text{K}}/R_{4\,\text{K}}$, a measure of a metal's purity. See [The Wiedemann–Franz law](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-wf).
- **Thermal conductance ($G$) and time constant ($\tau$).** $G$ is the heat flow per kelvin through a link; an object of heat capacity $C$ relaxes to its bath with $\tau = C/G$. See [The cooling time constant](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-tau).
- **Heat sinking.** Thermally anchoring a wire or part to an intermediate cryostat stage so its heat is removed there. See [Thermal conductivity](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-conduct) and [Keeping heat out: wiring](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-wiring).
- **Wet and dry cooling.** Cooling with cryogenic liquids (nitrogen, helium) versus closed-cycle cryocoolers driven by electricity. See [How to cool things down](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-cool).
- **Pulse tube cryocooler.** A closed-cycle refrigerator with no moving cold parts, typically in two stages near 50 K and 3 K. See [The pulse tube cryocooler](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-pulsetube).
- **Dilution refrigerator.** A continuous refrigerator that cools by moving helium-3 across the phase boundary in a helium-3/helium-4 mixture, reaching about 10 mK. See [The dilution refrigerator](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-dr).
- **Mixing chamber and still.** The coldest stage of a dilution refrigerator, where the cooling happens, and the stage near 0.7 K where helium-3 is evaporated and pumped away. See [How dilution cooling works](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-dr-physics).
- **Adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator (ADR).** A single-shot refrigerator that cools a paramagnetic salt by ramping down a magnetic field. See [The adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator](lectures/week04.qmd#sec-adr).
